title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 7 of Grothendieck's notes on the algebraic formalism of correspondences and the standard conjectures. Section 6 dealt with an abstract graded module M^* (degrees 0..2n) carrying a Lefschetz operator L of degree 2. In that setting the hard Lefschetz conditions let one define:
- the primitive decomposition M^j = ⊕_α L^α P^{j-2α};
- the projectors π_{j,α} onto L^α P^{j-2α};
- the canonical 'inverse' Λ, characterised by (6.15): LΛ = 1 − Σ_{i≤n} π_{i,0} and ΛL = 1 − Σ_{j≥n} π_{j,0}.

On the previous page Grothendieck builds a universal model. M_0 is a free Z-module of rank 2n with a non-degenerate alternating form ξ_0. One takes M_0^* = ΛM_0, L_0 = ξ_0∧· and Λ_0 = contraction with the dual form ξ_0^*.

On this page he defines 𝔏, the algebra generated by the 'matrix units' φ_i^{β,α}, for 0 ≤ i ≤ n and α, β in the admissible range.
- φ_i^{β,α} maps the α-th Lefschetz layer L^αP^i to the β-th layer L^βP^i.
- For α ≤ β it is L_0^{β−α} π_{i+2α,α} = π_{i+2β,β} L_0^{β−α}.
- For α ≥ β it is Λ_0^{α−β} π_{i+2α,α}.
- They multiply like matrix units: φ_i^{β,α} φ_{i'}^{β',α'} = 0 unless i = i' and α = β', and the product is then a single φ_i.

Hence 𝔏 ≅ ∏_{i=0}^{n} M_{n−i+1}(base ring). This is a product of full matrix algebras, one for each primitive degree i, with the string length n−i+1 as matrix size. It is the image of U(sl_2) acting on a Lefschetz module of weight range 2n, enlarged by the degree projectors.

Grothendieck observes that this multiplication table depends only on n, not on (M, ξ). So 𝔏 is a universal 'Lefschetz algebra'.

Proposition. Let M^* be graded and ℰ ⊂ End(M^*) a graded subring containing L ∈ ℰ^{(2)} and the degree projectors π_i. The following are equivalent:
(i) M^* satisfies the Lefschetz conditions of n°6, and the canonical Λ (and hence the π_{i,α}) lies in ℰ.
(ii) There is a ring homomorphism φ: 𝔏 → ℰ with L_0 ↦ L and π_i ↦ π_i.
The next page adds that φ is then unique and sends Λ_0 ↦ Λ, π_{i,α} ↦ π_{i,α}, φ_i^{β,α} ↦ φ_i^{β,α}.

The proof of (ii)⇒(i) transports the identities (Λ_0^{n−i}L_0^{n−i} − 1)π_i = 0 through φ.

Purpose: applied with ℰ = algebraic correspondences on a variety X, this recasts Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X), together with the Künneth projectors π_i, as the existence of an algebra map from a fixed universal semisimple algebra into correspondences. Equivalently, it is an action of the Lefschetz/sl_2 structure on the motive by algebraic cycles.
errors: Integrality: over Z the contraction Λ_0 = ξ_0^*⌟ is the sl_2 lowering operator, not the canonical Λ of (6.15). Already for rank 4, Λ_0L_0(1) = Λ_0(e12+e34) = 2 ≠ 1. More generally L_0^n(1) = n!·(volume form), so L_0^{n−i} is not unimodular over Z. The canonical Λ, the projectors π_{i,α} and the φ_i^{β,α} with α>β therefore need denominators (factorials). The claim that 𝔏 is a free Z-module with these generators inside End_Z(ΛM_0), and that Λ_0 'is the canonical operation (6.15)', is wrong over Z. It holds over Q, or over Z[1/n!]-type rings, or with a divided-power/Kostant-form normalisation of the generators. The left-margin note about Z ('Z vu ici engendré par ...') may be Grothendieck flagging exactly this; it is illegible.
Index range: as written, 0≤α,β≤2n−i. Mathematically the Lefschetz string over primitive degree i has length n−i+1, so it should be 0≤α,β≤n−i. Probably a slip.

Product rule: as transcribed, the product is φ_i^{β',α}. With the convention that φ^{β,α} maps layer α to layer β, the nonzero case requires α = β' and yields φ_i^{β,α'}. The indices on the page appear muddled, and the crossed-out variants show he was still fixing conventions.

ideas.what: Universal Lefschetz algebra 𝔏 with basis of matrix units φ_i^{β,α}, isomorphic to ∏_i M_{n−i+1}; its multiplication depends only on n.
ideas.modern_name: Image of U(sl_2) / Lefschetz algebra; semisimple algebra of an sl_2-representation with isotypic decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical sl_2/Lefschetz theory (Chern, Weil); in the motivic context Kleiman (1968), later Looijenga–Lunts (1997), Y. André (2004 book)
ideas.where_published: Not in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), which only states conjecture B via Λ

ideas.what: Equivalence: the Lefschetz conditions plus Λ (and the Lefschetz projectors) lying in a graded ring ℰ of endomorphisms ⇔ existence of a (unique) homomorphism 𝔏 → ℰ sending L_0 to L and π_i to π_i.
ideas.modern_name: Standard conjecture B (with C) ⇔ algebraic sl_2-action / Lefschetz decomposition of the motive by correspondences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kleiman (1968, 1994) for B⇔ algebraicity of Λ and of the Lefschetz projectors; Künnemann (1993) for abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: unsure; the idea is implicit in Grothendieck 1969 and Kleiman 1968

ideas.what: Universal model: exterior algebra of a symplectic free module of rank 2n as the generic Lefschetz module (abelian-variety cohomology type).
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology of abelian varieties as model hard-Lefschetz algebra; symplectic/Howe-type duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Lieberman (1968) used this for abelian varieties

missed.claim: Grothendieck attempts an integral (over Z) version of the universal Lefschetz algebra, intending to formulate standard conjecture B integrally or at least independently of the coefficient ring. The naive integral version fails because of factorial denominators. A correct integral form would use divided powers (the Kostant Z-form of sl_2), which he did not do.
missed.quote: 𝔏 est un module libre sur ℤ, engendré par les φ_i^{β,α} ... ne dépend pas du choix de M, ξ, ni de l'anneau
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and torsion versions of Lefschetz-type standard conjectures (with Z or Z_ℓ coefficients, or for Chow motives with integral coefficients) are a live but marginal topic. This page shows Grothendieck considered the question, but the attempt is flawed and the idea is minor.

deep.surprise_reason: The reformulation of conjecture B as a homomorphism from a universal semisimple 'Lefschetz algebra' is natural and is essentially known (Kleiman; later sl_2/Looijenga–Lunts/André viewpoints). The only distinctive feature is the attempted Z-integral framing, which contains an integrality error rather than a hidden result.
transcription_corrections: The marginal note and the conditions refer to 'n° 6' (section 6), not 'n=6': 'Les φ_i^{βα} et leurs multiplications données au n° 6' and 'conditions des th. du n° 6'.
Index range in the image reads '0≤α,β≤2n−i' next to '0≤i≤n'; mathematically n−i is intended.
The product rule is partly illegible; the intended nonzero value is φ_i^{β,α'} when α = β' (the transcription gives φ_i^{β',α}).
'(i) L'inverse ... de M^*' likely reads 'L'opérateur L de M^* satisfait les conditions de Lefschetz et l'opérateur Λ ... est dans ℰ'.
